key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 steel, delivering the best resistance among the tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: This coating could improve oxidation protection for SA516 boiler steel exposed to high-temperature air.
method: Apply Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterize microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports severe oxide spalling and cracking on bare steel, while improved coating performance was attributed to protective oxide formation, reduced porosity, and increased microhardness.
watch_item: Results cover laboratory air oxidation over 50 cycles; long-term performance in actual boiler atmospheres remains unverified.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
